overview.originName: NLK (Hungarian initials; full name not cited in sources).
overview.description: NLK (Czech variant) is a unique two-phase beating and shedding game from the Czech Republic. It combines elements of 'accumulation' (Phase One) and 'beating' (Phase Two). Players first build stacks of cards by placing one rank higher than the opponent's top card, and then use these accumulated cards to play a trick-beating game where the goal is to empty your hand.
overview.deck: Variable (32 to 52 cards depending on players)

history.origins: Part of the Central European 'Beating' (Pebble/Durak-like) family. It evolved specifically in the Czech Republic as a more social and chaotic variant than standard Trick-taking.
timeline: Early 20th Century: NLK becomes popular in Bohemian taverns
1990s: Rules are standardized for competitive play in Czech card associations
Present: Still a favorite in Czech pubs and social gatherings
21st Century: Often played as a drinking game where losers buy the next round
history.evolution: The 'Chain Reaction' mechanic in Phase One is its most distinctive modern feature.
history.cultural: Reflects the Czech love for 'Pivnice' (pub) culture where games must be easy to start but hard to master.

setup.players: Four to nine players. The primary source describes it as best for about six players. Four players use a 32-card pack; five use 36 cards, six use 40, and so on, adding one more rank (four cards) for each extra player up to nine with a full 52-card pack. Deal and play are anticlockwise; the player to dealer's right begins phase one.
setup.deck: 32 cards for 4 players; add ranks for more players. Rank: Ace (High) to 7/2 (Low).
setup.dealing: Each player starts with one card face-up. Remainder is the 'Talon'.

rules.objective: Avoid being the last player with cards in Phase Two.
rules.gameplay: Phase One: players take turns drawing from the talon and placing cards on their face-up stack; they may give away cards that fit (next rank above) on others' stacks or place drawn cards there, building chain reactions. Phase Two: the last talon card sets trump; players play to tricks by beating the previous card (higher same suit or trump) or picking up the lowest card; last player with cards loses.
keyRules: Phase One: build stack, give away cards that fit (next rank higher)
Phase Two: beat with higher same suit, or pick up lowest
Chain reactions possible in Phase One

strategy.basic: In Phase One, your goal is a SMALL stack. Don't hoard cards. Every time an opponent plays a 6, check if you have a 7 to dump on them immediately. Chains are your best friendâ€”try to move 3 or 4 cards off your stack in a single turn.
strategy.intermediate: Phase Two Suit Control: Since you must follow suit and beat the card, observe what suits your opponents are discarding. If you see many Spades being played early, save your high Spades for the end-game when others are out and you can win tricks freely.
strategy.advanced: The 'Low Card Pickup' Trap: In Phase Two, if you can't beat a high card, you pick up the LOWEST card of the trick. Sometimes, it's beneficial to pick up a '2' or '3' early if it gives you a sequence you can use to beat other cards later. It's 'Losing to Win'.
tips: In Phase One, Aces are dangerous because they can only be covered by 2s (wrapping around)
Always track how many cards are left in the Talon. When it's low, start playing aggressively to dump your stack

difficulty.easy: Fails to see give-away opportunities in Phase One; picks up high cards in Phase Two.
difficulty.medium: Excellent chain-reaction logic; manages suit-balance in hand.
difficulty.hard: Expert at 'Stack Minimization'; perfectly times the Phase Two pickups to build a winning final hand; master of the chain dump.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Higher same suit or any trump beats.

validPlays.notes: Beat previous card with higher same suit or trump; or pick up lowest card in trick instead.

edgeCases.text: Once you have drawn from the talon in Phase One, you cannot give away cards from your own stack that turn.
Phase One ends when the last card is drawn from the talon; that card determines trump for Phase Two and is shown to all; the drawer keeps it and leads Phase Two.
In Phase Two you may always pick up the lowest card in the trick instead of playing; some tricks may go several times around before completion.
When the player due to lead has no cards (won the previous trick with their last card), the lead passes to the next player in rotation.
The hand can end in the middle of a trick (e.g. two players each with one card: the leader wins even if the other could beat the led card).

customActions.description: Draw the top card from the talon and place it face up on top of your stack. You may first give away cards from your stack or place drawn talon cards on other players' stacks if they fit (next rank above). Once you draw, you cannot move cards from your own stack this turn. Turn ends when you place a card on your own pile.
customActions.constraints: Legal only in Phase One. You may optionally give away from stack or place drawn cards on others' stacks if the card fits (next rank above; lowest rank fits on ace). Eventually you must place one card on your own pile to end the turn.

customActions.description: At the start of your turn, move the top card from your stack onto another player's stack if it fits (next rank above their top card; lowest rank fits on ace). You may then give away the next card in your stack if it fits somewhere. You can continue as long as there is a legal placement. You are never obliged to give away.
customActions.constraints: Legal only before drawing from the talon in Phase One. A card fits if it is the next rank above the target (any suit). Once you have drawn from the talon this turn, you cannot give from your stack.

customActions.description: Play a card that beats the previous card played to the trick: either a higher card of the same suit or any trump. There is no obligation to follow suit; you may trump even when holding the led suit.
customActions.constraints: Legal in Phase Two when it is your turn to play to the trick. You must beat the previous card (higher same suit or trump) or instead choose to pick up the lowest card in the trick.

customActions.description: If you are unable or unwilling to beat the previous card played to the trick, you must pick up the lowest card in the trick and add it to your hand. It is then the next player's turn to play to the trick. You may always choose this instead of playing a card.
customActions.constraints: Legal in Phase Two when it is your turn to play to the trick. You can always pick up the lowest card instead of playing. After you pick up, the next player in rotation leads or plays to the trick.

engine.handRankingSystem: Beat by higher same suit or trump; no hand ranking. Last player with cards loses.
engine.deckDescription: A 32-card French deck formed by removing ranks 2 through 6 from a standard pack, leaving 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, and Ace in each of the four French suits.
engine.suitDescription: French suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. All four suits are used; in Phase Two one suit is trump (determined by the last card drawn from the talon).
engine.rankDescription: Stripped 32-card ranking from high to low: Ace, King, Queen, Jack, 10, 9, 8, 7. The lowest rank fits on the ace (wrap). With more players, more ranks are added (e.g. 36 cards for 5 players, 40 for 6, up to full 52 for 9 players).
engine.dealPattern: One card face-up per player; remainder forms the talon (face down in the centre).
